overview: Regional Ocean Partnerships are groups of coastal states, working with federal agencies and tribes, that coordinate on shared ocean and coast issues such as fisheries, pollution, and coastal planning, with funding from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). This bill extends their federal funding authorization through 2031, setting amounts of about $10.6 million to $11 million a year for 2028 through 2031. It bars the partnerships from using these funds to develop regulatory proposals, model regulations, or compliance programs. It also requires a new report on the partnerships within five years, updates the list of member states, and renames the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America in the law. As of September 14, 2026, it had been approved by a Senate committee and placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say ocean and coastal problems cross state lines, and keeping these partnerships funded helps states coordinate and share data at a modest cost, while the new limit keeps them out of rulemaking.
against: Critics say the new ban on regulatory work may limit what the partnerships can do to help states address coastal problems, and some may question extending federal spending on coordination groups.
